discovery: Programmable arrays of individually trapped neutral atoms in optical tweezers, coupled via Rydberg interactions, for quantum simulation and computation

nominees.name: Philippe Grangier
nominees.affiliation: Institut d'Optique Graduate School, CNRS, Université Paris-Saclay, France

nominees.name: Antoine Browaeys
nominees.affiliation: Institut d'Optique Graduate School, CNRS, Université Paris-Saclay, France

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / quantum optics
motivation: Controlling single quantum objects one by one is the foundation of the second quantum revolution. Grangier and Browaeys first trapped and manipulated individual atoms in microscopic optical tweezers (2001), then demonstrated the Rydberg blockade between two atoms and their entanglement (2009), a mechanism proposed by Lukin and co-workers. Browaeys and Lukin then scaled this approach into deterministic, reconfigurable arrays of hundreds of atoms. With these arrays they observed quantum magnetism, many-body scars, topological spin liquids and high-fidelity parallel entangling gates, culminating in logical qubits with error correction. This platform turns entanglement, once a philosophical puzzle, into a programmable resource. It joins conceptual clarity, elegant optics and transformative technology. It has become a leading route to quantum simulation and fault-tolerant quantum computing, and it opens new tests of many-body quantum physics.
